title: Cross-linking/MS-analysis of Thr72-phosphorylated Rab8A and PPM1H (D288A) complex
author: Pawel Lis
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bv2en8be

Submit the .mgf files to search using MeroX software against PPM1H and Rab-8A protein sequences to identify potential cross-linked peptides (He et al. 2015). Digestive enzyme, trypsin, trypsin and AspN, or trypsin and GluC, were selected according to the experimental setup. 3 maximum missed cleavages with peptide length ranged from 3 to 50 were applied. Carbamidomethylation at Cysteine residue was set as fixed modification; while oxidation at methionine residue and deamidation at asparagine residue were included in variable modification. DSBU cross-linker was selected with specificity cross-linked sites at Lysine, Serine, Threonine, and Tyrosine residues. 10 ppm and 20 ppm were used to filter the mass error in precursor ion (MS1) and fragment ion (MS2) scans. Only ions with signal-to-noise ratio high than 2 were used for database search. RISEUP searching mode was applied, minimum 2 fragments per peptide and 5% false discovery rate (FDR) were required for a cross-linked peptide identification.

steps.title: Prepare dialysis buffer
steps.instruction: Make 500 mL of 40 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 2 mM MgCl₂ buffer in a beaker, add a magnetic stir bar and stir gently at room temperature.

steps.title: Dialyze proteins into HEPES buffer
steps.instruction: Pipette up to 0.5 mL of each protein (PPM1H and pRab8A) into separate Diacon dialysis tubes, float the tubes in the buffer beaker for 2 h at room temperature; then transfer the floating rack to a fresh beaker containing 500 mL of the same buffer and stir gently overnight at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare protein mixture for cross‑linking
steps.instruction: In a total volume of 15.5 µL of the HEPES buffer, combine Thr72‑phosphorylated Rab8A at 35 µM (~0.7 mg mL⁻¹, 20 kDa) and PPM1H at 28 µM (~1.4 mg mL⁻¹, 50 kDa) to obtain a 1.25‑fold molar excess of Rab8A over PPM1H. Adjust the individual volumes according to the concentrations measured after dialysis.

steps.title: Pre‑incubate protein mixture
steps.instruction: Mix the protein solution gently and incubate at 30 °C for 1 h, then keep at room temperature for an additional 10 min.

steps.title: Prepare DSBU cross‑linker stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 mg of DSBU in 15.5 µL anhydrous DMSO to obtain a 300 mM stock, vortex briefly, keep on ice and use within 5 min.

steps.title: Add cross‑linker to protein mixture
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 µL of the DSBU stock to the 15.5 µL protein solution, mix gently; the final reaction volume is 16 µL with DSBU at 9.375 mM (≈250‑fold excess to pRab8A and ≈335‑fold excess to PPM1H).

steps.title: Cross‑link and quench reaction
steps.instruction: Incubate the cross‑linking mixture for 10 min at room temperature, then add 2 µL of 1 M Tris pH 8.8 to quench and mix gently.

steps.title: Add sample buffer and run SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Add 7 µL of 4× NuPAGE™ LDS Sample Buffer (contains lithium dodecyl sulfate, SERVA Blue G250, phenol red) to the quenched reaction, vortex, and load 6 µL aliquots of each of the four samples (A–D) onto a 4–12 % gradient NuPAGE Bis‑Tris gel. Run the gel at 70 V for 20 min, then at 120 V until the dye front exits. Do **not** add reducing agent or heat the samples before electrophoresis.

steps.title: Fix the gel
steps.instruction: Prepare fixing solution (10 % v/v glacial acetic acid in 50 % v/v methanol) by mixing 5 mL acetic acid, 25 mL methanol and 20 mL milli‑Q water. Incubate the gel in this solution for 10 min at room temperature with gentle shaking, then discard the fixing solution.

steps.title: Initial gel staining (Stainer A)
steps.instruction: Prepare staining solution (20 % v/v methanol, 20 % v/v Stainer A, 5 % v/v Stainer B) by mixing 10 mL Stainer A, 10 mL methanol and 22.5 mL milli‑Q water (do **not** add Stainer B yet). Incubate the gel in this solution for 10 min at room temperature with gentle shaking.

steps.title: Develop stain with Stainer B
steps.instruction: Add 2.5 mL Stainer B directly to the solution containing the gel and incubate for 2–4 h at room temperature with gentle shaking.

steps.title: Rinse, image and excise bands
steps.instruction: Rinse the gel with milli‑Q water at least three times over a period of ≥4 h or overnight while gently shaking. Image the gel, identify the pRab8A‑PPM1H cross‑linked band (≈140 kDa) and the PPM1H dimer band (≈100 kDa), and excise each band with a sterile scalpel. Cut each excised band into ~1 mm³ pieces and place the pieces into separate low‑binding 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes (one tube per digestion condition A, B, C, D).

steps.title: Dehydrate gel pieces
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL acetonitrile to each tube, incubate at room temperature for 10 min to dehydrate the gel pieces.

steps.title: Reduce disulfides with DTT
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of freshly prepared 10 mM DTT (add a second 50 µL if needed to fully cover the gel pieces) and incubate at 56 °C for 30 min while mixing at 1200 rpm.

steps.title: Alkylate cysteines with IAA
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL acetonitrile, incubate 10 min at room temperature without shaking to dehydrate again. Prepare fresh 55 mM iodoacetamide (IAA) in 100 mM ammonium bicarbonate (ABC). Add 50–100 µL of this IAA solution to fully cover the gel pieces, cover the tubes with aluminium foil, and incubate 20 min at room temperature while mixing at 1200 rpm. Then incubate another 10 min at room temperature without shaking to dehydrate. Discard the supernatant as toxic waste.

steps.title: Wash and prepare for digestion
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of 50 mM ABC in 50 % v/v acetonitrile, incubate 30 min at room temperature without shaking. Add 500 µL acetonitrile (do not discard the previous supernatant), incubate 10 min at room temperature to dehydrate the pieces.

steps.title: Prepare protease solutions
steps.instruction: Make fresh protease stocks on ice: 80 µL of 50 ng µL⁻¹ Trypsin in milli‑Q water; 20 µL of 20 ng µL⁻¹ AspN in milli‑Q water; 20 µL of 50 ng µL⁻¹ GluC in milli‑Q water.

steps.title: Add proteases and digest overnight
steps.instruction:
For each tube add proteases as follows (add 25 mM ABC if gel pieces are not fully covered):
- Sample A: 20 µL Trypsin.
- Sample B: 20 µL Trypsin.
- Sample C: 20 µL Trypsin + 20 µL AspN.
- Sample D: 20 µL Trypsin + 20 µL GluC.
Incubate all four samples overnight at 30 °C with mixing at 1200 rpm.

steps.title: Elute peptides from gel
steps.instruction: Prepare peptide elution solution (1.67 % v/v TFA in acetonitrile; mix 2 vol ACN with 1 vol 5 % TFA). Add 100 µL of this solution to each tube, incubate 15 min at 37 °C while mixing at 1200 rpm, then transfer the supernatant to a fresh low‑binding tube, avoiding any gel fragments. Add a second 100 µL of elution solution to the same gel pieces, incubate again 15 min at 37 °C, transfer the supernatant and combine with the first eluate.

steps.title: Enrich sample B on MCX cartridge
steps.instruction: To the tube labelled B, add 1 mL of 4 % v/v H₃PO₄ aqueous solution and sonicate in a room‑temperature water bath for 30 min. Wash an MCX cartridge sequentially with 2 mL methanol, then 2 mL 4 % H₃PO₄. Load the acid‑treated sample onto the cartridge using a 1000 µL pipette. Wash the cartridge with 500 µL 4 % H₃PO₄, then with 500 µL 10 % MeOH containing 0.1 % FA. Elute low‑charged peptides with 500 µL 500 mM NH₄OAc in 40 % MeOH + 0.1 % FA, and elute high‑charged peptides with 700 µL 2000 mM NH₄OAc in 80 % MeOH + 0.1 % FA.

steps.title: Prepare peptides for LC‑MS/MS
steps.instruction: Vacuum‑dry all peptide eluates, then re‑suspend each in 30 µL of 3 % v/v acetonitrile, 0.1 % v/v FA. Sonicate in a room‑temperature water bath for 30 min.

steps.title: Nano‑LC separation
steps.instruction:
Load 3–14 µL of each peptide solution onto the nano‑HPLC system. Trap peptides on a pre‑column (Acclaim PepMap™ 100, C18, 100 µm × 2 cm, 5 µm, 100 Å) using 0.1 % v/v TFA. Separate on an analytical column (PepMap™ RSLC C18, 75 µm × 50 cm, 2 µm, 100 Å) maintained at 45 °C, at a flow rate of 300 nL min⁻¹, using the following linear gradient of solvent B (80 % ACN, 0.1 % FA):
1 % → 35 % B for 1 h 30 min,
35 % → 85 % B for 5 min,
85 % B hold for 10 min,
85 % → 1 % B for 1 min,
1 % B hold for 14 min.

steps.title: Acquire MS/MS data
steps.instruction: Perform data‑dependent acquisition on an Orbitrap Exploris™ 480: MS scan 375–1500 m/z, resolution 120 000, AGC 300 %, max injection 100 ms. Select the top 10 precursors (charge 2‑8, intensity > 1 × 10⁴) with a 1.2 Da isolation window. Fragment by stepped HCD at normalized collision energies 27 %, 30 % and 33 %. MS/MS resolution 15 000, AGC 200 %, max injection 250 ms. Apply dynamic exclusion of 60 s with a 2 ppm window.

steps.title: Process data and validate cross‑links
steps.instruction: Convert the acquired .RAW files to .mgf format using RawConverter software. Verify candidate cross‑linked peptides, retaining only those with a score > 50.
